section: On the day of new student enrollment

conversation.speaker: dialogue
conversation.text:
Police: On the day of new student registration, you spoke with a staff member from the subdistrict office on the phone, right?
Police: Do you live with your daughter?
Respondent: New student registration? That day...
Respondent: What did my daughter say again... It seemed she said she had a cold? Yes, that should be it.
Respondent: Ah, I remember now.
Respondent: I had been keeping the registration date in mind and later asked her whether she went.
Respondent: We don’t live together. I live nearby and come over to see her whenever I have time.
Respondent: After all...
Respondent: If she stays home alone, she tends to overthink. After a long time, she gets trapped in her emotions and can’t get out.
Respondent: A few days ago, when I went to her home, I happened to receive a call from the subdistrict office.
Respondent: That person asked the same questions as you.
Respondent: I said our granddaughter is doing very well. I will raise my own granddaughter properly. There’s no need for you to worry.
Respondent: I said, Officer.
Respondent: It’s not a big deal if a child doesn’t go to school. Is it necessary to make such a fuss?
